title: Number to English Words

concept.title: Work in groups of three digits
body: English reads a number in groups of three digits, from the left: "one billion, two hundred thirty-four million, ..." The words for a group of three digits are always built the same way, and the group is followed by its scale word (Thousand, Million, Billion). So write a helper for **numbers below 1000** and call it for each group.

body.code:
def three(x):
    words = []
    if x >= 100: words += [ONES[x // 100], "Hundred"]; x %= 100
    if x >= 20: words.append(TENS[x // 10]); x %= 10
    if x > 0: words.append(ONES[x])      # 1..19 have their own words
    return words

body: Take the groups from the right with `n % 1000` and `n // 1000`, skip groups that are zero (no "Zero Thousand"), and put the results in the right order at the end. The number 0 itself is the special case "Zero".

statement: Write a non-negative integer in English words. Use capitalised words separated by single spaces, no "and" and no hyphens: `123` is `One Hundred Twenty Three`, `1000010` is `One Million Ten`. The scale words are Thousand, Million and Billion. Zero is written as `Zero`.

examples.output: Twelve Thousand Three Hundred Forty Five
examples.note: Twelve Thousand Three Hundred Forty Five
The zero thousands group is skipped.

hints: Handle numbers below 1000 with a helper: hundreds, then tens, then ones.
The numbers 1 to 19 have their own words; 20, 30, ..., 90 are in a separate list.
Split the number into groups of three digits from the right, skip empty groups, and add the scale word to each used group.

explanation: A number is a sequence of three-digit groups. Each group is spelled with the same small helper and followed by its scale word; empty groups are skipped.
solution.complexity: Time O(number of digits), space O(1).

code.python:
ONES = ["", "One", "Two", "Three", "Four", "Five", "Six", "Seven", "Eight", "Nine", "Ten", "Eleven",
        "Twelve", "Thirteen", "Fourteen", "Fifteen", "Sixteen", "Seventeen", "Eighteen", "Nineteen"]
TENS = ["", "", "Twenty", "Thirty", "Forty", "Fifty", "Sixty", "Seventy", "Eighty", "Ninety"]
SCALE = ["", "Thousand", "Million", "Billion"]


def three(x):
    words = []
    if x >= 100:
        words += [ONES[x // 100], "Hundred"]
        x %= 100
    if x >= 20:
        words.append(TENS[x // 10])
        x %= 10
    if x > 0:
        words.append(ONES[x])
    return words

n = int(input())

if n == 0:
    print("Zero")
else:
    parts = []
    unit = 0
    while n > 0:
        chunk = n % 1000
        if chunk:
            words = three(chunk)
            if unit:
                words.append(SCALE[unit])
            parts.append(words)
        n //= 1000
        unit += 1
    print(" ".join(w for part in reversed(parts) for w in part))
